FN-3PSQLZZ-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 271
Committee: Agriculture and Forestry Sponsor: Representative Shane Stringer
Analyst: Mathieu Fuller Date: 01/20/2026
House Bill 271 as introduced would authorize the Department of Conservation and Natural
Resources to issue new disabled resident lifetime hunting, freshwater fishing, and saltwater
fishing licenses with $25 fees for residents over the age of 50 years old, and $45 fees for those
under the age of 50. This bill also provides that these fees may be adjusted periodically based on
the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI), as currently provided by law for
certain other hunting and fishing licenses.
This bill would increase receipts to the Alabama Game and Fish Endowment Fund and Marine
Resources Endowment Fund, while correspondingly decrease receipts to the Game and Fish
Fund and the Marine Resources Fund, by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number
of disabled resident lifetime licenses purchased that would otherwise have been purchased
annually, as provided below:

Finally, this bill allows the department to assess an issuance fee of $1 for each license, which is
also subject to the periodic CPI adjustment. Current law provides that this fee may be retained
by the judge of probate, issuing officer, or other authorized license agent
